adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 99.3. Memorial Day (Mon) is a strong driver with noise-adjusted lift of x1.18 from two past occurrences. No promotion or price change this week (price unchanged at $9.88). No recent promotion in the past 2 weeks, so no pantry-loading effect. The classical model suggests 0.93, but this overcorrects by applying a -21% post-promo penalty without evidence of a prior promotion. No such event occurred. Thus, only the Memorial Day effect applies. Noise-adjusted lift is credible and consistent. No need to shrink further. No uncertainty in driver size. Spread remains baseline.

  shelf price: 9.88 (+0.0% vs regular price 9.88)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 99.3 | 5%-95%: 63.7 - 219.9 | 10%-90%: 66.2 - 189.7

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-21% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
